//: THE BUDGET IS ENFORCED BY `replay/tools/build_browser_bundle.mjs`, WHICH FAILS THE BUILD.
A number in a comment is not a budget. This file is data the builder reads and the check
re-reads, so the two cannot come to disagree about what was promised.
WHAT `eager` MEANS HERE, precisely, because it is the whole point: the entry output plus the
transitive closure of its STATIC (`import-statement`) edges. An output reached only by a
`dynamic-import` edge is LAZY — the browser fetches it when the code path runs and not before.
esbuild marks split targets with `entryPoint` too, so `entryPoint` is NOT the discriminator and
using it would count 8.2 MB of lazily-fetched barretenberg as eager.
WHY 1,200,000. Measured eager on 2026-08-30 is 1,107,050 bytes across four files, so this is
~8% headroom: enough that ordinary churn in `replay/src` does not fail a build, tight enough
that the regressions worth catching are caught. It is a CEILING and not a target.
AND THE BYTE BUDGET IS THE WEAKER OF THE TWO GUARDS, DELIBERATELY. The regression that matters
is STRUCTURAL — one of the two 4 MB barretenberg blobs becoming eagerly imported — and a byte
budget catches that only incidentally, by being smaller than 4 MB. `lazyRequired` names those
two directly, so the property is asserted rather than inferred from a size. DD-11's demand is
'a page which only executes a public transaction never fetches the barretenberg wasm at all',
which is a statement about WHICH chunk a module is in, not about how many bytes there are.
`maxEagerFiles` exists so a NEW eager chunk is visible even when it is small. Four chunks
totalling 1.1 MB and five totalling 1.1 MB are different facts about the graph.

M-NOTE 2026-08-30, SECOND MEASUREMENT: adding the page entry (`browser-demo/replay_in_page.ts`) to this pass moved the library entry's eager set from 4 chunks / 1,107,050 bytes to 5 / 1,108,275 — esbuild's splitting is a function of which entries reach which module, which is the same mechanism BROWSER-PACKAGING.md records moving its figures three times. Nothing changed CLASS: the two barretenberg blobs are still lazy, which is what `lazyRequired` exists to say. `maxEagerFiles` is now exactly met, deliberately: a sixth eager chunk should require a decision, not slip through.

measured.note: The BUDGET is the LIBRARY entry's. The page additionally pulls in ct-host and the browser AVM loader, which a consumer of the library does not, so it is reported and not budgeted.
